Every block lists three such determinants, each with a multiplier written to its right. It then begins expanding the weighted sum to show that it vanishes. In each case this is one component of the elementary identity
[r1,r2]·r + [r2,r]·r1 + [r,r1]·r2 = 0 for any third vector r.

Block 1 (r = r3, first components):
(αδ−βγ)·α' + (βα'−αβ')·γ − (δα'−γβ')·α = 0.
Expansion: αδα' − βγα' + βγα' − αγβ' − αδα' + αγβ' = 0. Gauss writes the start: a cancelled term, then −βγα' + αγβ'.

Block 2 (r = r4, first components):
(αδ−βγ)·γ' − (αδ'−βγ')·γ + (γδ'−δγ')·α = 0.
Expansion: αδγ' − βγγ' − αγδ' + βγγ' + αγδ' − αδγ' = 0. Gauss writes αγδ' − βγγ' and αγ'δ.

Block 3 (r = r4, second components):
(αδ−βγ)·δ' − (αδ'−βγ')·δ + (γδ'−δγ')·β = 0.
Gauss starts the expansion with αδδ' − βγδ'.

Block 4 (r = r3, second components):
(αδ−βγ)·β' + (βα'−αβ')·δ − (δα'−γβ')·β = 0.
Gauss starts with αβ'δ − (cancelled βγβ') + βδα'.

Together the blocks give the complete set of linear (three-term) relations between the 2x2 minors of the 2x4 array
(α β α' β' ; γ δ γ' δ')
and its entries.
